questions.q: What happens to the flow of electricity when you move a switch to the "OFF" position?
questions.a: The circuit is broken (opened), which stops the flow of current. A student who says "it still flows" confuses the term "open" with "open path," failing to realize that an open circuit is a disconnected one.

questions.q: If you have a battery, a bulb, and a switch connected in a loop, and the bulb is not glowing, what is the most likely state of the switch?
questions.a: The switch is likely "open." A student who says "the battery is dead" ignores the functional purpose of a switch, which is the primary control component in the circuit.

questions.q: You are drawing a circuit diagram to control a fan. If you want the fan to stay ON, should you draw the switch connection as touching or with a gap?
questions.a: You should draw it touching (closed). If a student draws a gap, they have not yet understood that a gap creates an open circuit, which prevents current from reaching the fan.

questions.q: Why is it dangerous to have a circuit without any switch at all?
questions.a: Without a switch, the circuit would remain permanently "on," wasting energy and posing a risk of overheating. If a student says "it wouldn't work," they fail to see that a permanent connection is a functional, albeit inefficient and unsafe, circuit.

questions.q: If a metal piece inside a switch is rusted and cannot touch the contact point, will the device turn on? Why?
questions.a: No, the device will not turn on because the rust acts as an insulator, preventing the circuit from closing. A student who thinks it might still turn on lacks an understanding that electricity requires a continuous conductive path.

questions.q: Design a simple "secret" switch for a cardboard toy box using only a paperclip, two thumbtacks, and wires. How would you arrange them?
questions.a: Place two thumbtacks on the cardboard with a small gap, connecting each to a wire. Attach one end of a paperclip to one thumbtack so it can swing to touch the other. A poor answer would fail to explain how the movement of the paperclip physically closes the gap.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: A switch is a mechanical device in an electrical circuit that controls the flow of current by physically connecting or ______ the conductive path.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered why the light in your room turns on only when you press a specific ______?
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to correctly identify whether a circuit is "open" or "closed" based on a visual diagram and explain why a device (like a bulb) will or will not function in each state.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Have you ever ______ why the light in your room turns on only when you press a specific button?
